answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a knoll as the anchor of the cost.
